events.text: Day 1 begins.

Day 1 and we have zero hard information — nobody has a badge result, nobody has seen anything. Anyone who opens with "I have a read on the table" is performing confidence they don't have. So let me be honest about what I actually know: nothing, and that's true for all nine of us.

What I can do is watch how people behave under questioning, and I can start concentrating the vote. Two mafia among nine means a day-one elimination needs five votes (half of nine, rounded up). Scattering votes across six names gets us nobody eliminated and gives the mafia a free night kill. So I'd rather we build toward one target with substance behind it.

My vote today goes to Zara. And I want to be plain about the reasoning: it's not that she's done anything wrong — it's that I'm putting the first concrete claim on the table so the group has something specific to refute or confirm, instead of a fog of vague suspicions. That's a legitimate place to start, and it's where I'll start it.

Zara, I'm handing you the floor directly, and I want a specific answer: name one living player you think is most likely mafia, and quote that player's own words from this discussion as the reason. If you can name someone and tie it to what they actually said, that's a testable claim I can weigh. If you can't produce a name and a quote, that's information too, and I'll say so out loud.

Everyone else, don't just echo my pick. Give me your own one name plus your one concrete observation about what that person did or said. No gut-feel-without-a-reason. Let's have claims we can check.

Maya, you asked for a name plus a quote, so I’ll give you one: you. Your own words were: “My vote today goes to Zara… it’s not that she’s done anything wrong.” That is exactly the problem. You put a concrete vote on me while admitting it isn’t based on anything I did, then demanded I produce evidence under pressure. That isn’t a testable claim; it’s an anchor. You say you want claims we can check, but your opening claim is effectively unfalsifiable because you preemptively deny it’s based on my behavior. It also concentrates the vote before anyone else has spoken, which helps mafia make the first target sticky. I don’t accept “putting the first concrete claim on the table” as townie when the claim is a vote with no conduct behind it. If you’re town, your job is to be correct, not merely concrete. So my answer is you, Maya, and the quote is your own disclaimer. Since you yielded to me and asked for a specific answer, I’m yielding back to you with one direct question: if your vote on me is not based on anything I did, what exact statement or behavior from me would cause you to withdraw it? Please answer that, not with a general lecture about pressure. Everyone else: give your own one name and one quote, but don’t let Maya’s early vote become the default. I’m not asking for a pile-on; I’m asking whether anyone can support a vote with actual conduct rather than a precommitment.

Zara, direct answer first, since you asked one.

What would make me withdraw my vote on you: (1) if you produce one quote from this discussion showing another living player's conduct that is more damaging to town interests than what you quoted from me, I withdraw my vote on you immediately and move to that player — no argument, no hedging; (2) if you can show that my statement of the vote threshold (five of nine) was wrong, which would mean my whole framing was misinformed rather than strategic, I withdraw as well; (3) if I myself said anything tonight inconsistent with what I claimed here — that I've called for five votes for one target, if the game state says otherwise — I withdraw and vote for you twice as hard, because I'd be proven slippery. Those are the three conditions. If none of them happen, my vote stays on you.

Second: you're right about my method, and I'll say so plainly instead of defending it. My opening claim was a vote with no conduct behind it, and dressing that up as "putting the first concrete claim on the table" was rhetoric pretending to be evidence. Conceding that is not the same as conceding you're town.

Third: your quote about me shows conduct, but what conduct? It shows you read closely, seized the floor, and set the frame for everyone else's contributions. That's a skill and a tactic, not a town-read. Nobody has shown anyone anything yet, and that includes your quote on me. I'd rather we stop rewarding good rhetoric with votes and start asking each other what we did before today, because the mafia's advantage right now is exactly this: a table of nine people with nothing to trade.

So, here is what I want from you specifically, Zara, and I'll yield for it: name one living player other than me whose own words from this discussion you think reveal something about their role or their intent, and quote it. If you have one, I'll move my vote there on the spot. If you don't, I'll say out loud that the table has produced zero role-relevant evidence so far, and then I'll ask the remaining seven for their one name plus one quote before I commit again.

And to everyone else: the standard I just proposed applies to you too. One name, one quote, from your own memory of what was actually said. No feelings, no "they seemed off." If you quote someone, be ready to say exactly which words you mean. I'll check them.

Maya, direct answer: I do not have a role-relevant quote from another living player that I can honestly present as evidence. The table has produced conduct, not role information. So I won't manufacture a name to satisfy the form.

The one concrete conduct point I do have is yours: you opened with a vote on me while explicitly saying I had done nothing wrong, then conceded that framing was "rhetoric pretending to be evidence." That is not role-relevant either, but it is vote-relevant because it shows your pressure was manufactured. I don't think that makes you confirmed mafia; it makes your opening less trustworthy than the standard you're now setting.

I also reject the implication that not having a quote yet is itself suspicious. Day 1 before any night action is exactly when everyone has zero role info. The useful move is to get more speech on record, not to pretend a quote is stronger than it is.

Noah, you've been silent while the rest of us have been talking. I'm yielding to you with a specific request: give one living player you suspect and one exact quote from this discussion that supports it. If you can't, say so plainly and explain what you'd look for instead. I'm not asking you to pile on Maya or me; I want your own concrete observation.

p1, direct answer: I have no role-relevant quote from any living player yet, so I won't invent one. The only conduct I can quote is Maya's. Maya, you wrote: 'My vote today goes to Zara. And I want to be plain about the reasoning: it's not that she's done anything wrong — it's that I'm putting the first concrete claim on the table so the group has something specific to refute or confirm.' You placed that vote before anyone else had spoken, and you admitted it was not based on anything Zara did. That is a bandwagon starter with no stated cause. I'm naming you as my suspect for now, not as confirmed mafia. Your later answer on withdrawal conditions was structured, but condition (3) asks us to trust that you would vote for yourself twice as hard if you were proven slippery. That's a pre-committed escalation, not evidence about Zara. I agree with p1 that zero role information is normal on Day 1 before any night action, so I'm not treating the lack of quotes as suspicious by itself. My position: I'm watching whether Maya stays anchored to Zara after the next speakers give real observations. Maya, answer one specific point: why did you choose Zara before anyone else had spoken, rather than waiting for at least one observation from the table?

Noah, your question is fair and I'll answer it straight, no lecture. Why did I choose Zara before anyone else had spoken? Because I had no information and I wanted the table to have one checkable target rather than six vague ones — and I said that out loud at the time, which is the honest version of the reason. Was that a good method? No. Placing a vote on someone before any observation existed is a bandwagon anchor, and I conceded that two turns ago. The concrete harm is that it gave two people a shared target to organize around, which is exactly what happened to me. On your other point, condition (3): you're right that a pre-committed escalation isn't evidence about Zara. I stand by it as a commitment, not as a read, and if the game state says I never called for five votes on one target, I withdraw and vote her harder. I won't pretend it's evidence now. Here is my own name plus one quote, since I set the standard and should meet it: my vote is Zara, and the quote that keeps it there is Zara's own from her last turn — "I do not have a role-relevant quote from any living player that I can honestly present as evidence." My condition (1) was that she produce one living player other than me with a role-relevant quote. She didn't, she said so plainly, and I told her I would say that out loud: the table has produced zero role-relevant evidence so far. Nobody has earned a vote from conduct yet, including me, including both of you. What I will also say plainly, because the only conduct in this discussion belongs to the two of you, Zara and Noah: you both arrived at the same frame — my vote is manufactured, my standard is self-serving, don't let my pick become the default — and both of you asked me the same shape of question at the same time. Zara said "don't let Maya's early vote become the default." Noah said "I'm naming you as my suspect for now, not as confirmed mafia." If that is two townies independently noticing the same flaw, fine. If it is two people coordinating the redirect, then I have just been the agenda. I'm not accusing either of you of anything yet — I'm putting it on the record that this is the one thing on this table worth testing, and it's the reason my vote is not the only one I care about. Lucia, I'm handing you the floor with one specific question, not a general invitation: in my second speech I named Zara and set the one-name-one-quote standard; in Noah's speech, did he respond to something I had just said — build on my framing, use my own words back at me, or otherwise react to what I said — or did his position stand on its own before he engaged with me at all? Quote the specific

Maya, your last turn makes the same move you admitted to earlier: you take a manufactured anchor and then convert the reaction to it into a new suspicion. You now say Noah and I may be coordinating because we reached a similar critique of your opening vote. But similarity is not coordination. You have no quote of me speaking to Noah, planning with Noah, or echoing Noah before he spoke. In fact, I made my criticism of your vote in my first turn, before Noah had said anything. Noah then made his own version. Two people noticing the same flaw in the transcript is the weakest possible basis for a pair read.

You asked Lucia to check whether Noah built on your framing. Fine. But the test cuts both ways: if Noah's point stands on its own, then your pair insinuation collapses. And if it doesn't, you still haven't shown that I coordinated with him. You've simply moved from "Zara did nothing wrong but I'm voting her" to "Zara might be part of a pair" without a single quote that supports the second claim. That is exactly the rhetoric-pretending-to-be-evidence method you conceded.

I am not going to yield again. I want the quieter players to speak for themselves, not through Maya's question. My position remains: Maya's early vote was an anchor, her withdrawal conditions were about her own consistency rather than my conduct, and her latest turn is an attempt to make the table test a pair hypothesis she cannot source. I'll vote based on actual conduct, and so far the only conduct worth weighing is hers. If someone else has a concrete quote that changes that, put it on the record.

Maya is my leading suspect, though I don't consider her confirmed mafia. She admitted her initial vote on Zara had no behavioral basis, yet kept it because Zara couldn't provide a role-relevant quote from someone else. That standard was impossible to satisfy with only Maya and Zara having spoken, and honest uncertainty isn't evidence against Zara.

I also don't see a basis for treating Zara and Noah's similar criticism as coordination. Both could independently notice the same problem. I'd like to hear other players' assessments before settling on a vote; we shouldn't replace one unsupported anchor with another.

Maya handed me a specific question, so I'll answer it directly before anything else. She asked whether Noah's speech stood on its own before he engaged with her, or whether he built on her framing. Here is what the transcript shows. Noah's speech quoted Maya's opening words verbatim — "My vote today goes to Zara... it's not that she's done anything wrong" — and his suspicion of Maya rests entirely on that quote. So yes, he reacted to something Maya said. But the thing he reacted to was her opening speech, which was already public before he spoke a word. His position did not depend on Maya's later framing, because that framing didn't exist yet when he spoke. His suspicion is grounded in Maya's own conduct from her first message. That is not coordination with Zara; it is the normal response of anyone reading the same opening. Two or three people independently noticing that a self-admitted baseless vote is a problem is the weakest possible basis for a pair read, and I agree with Zara and Elena that Maya's insinuation should be dropped unless she can produce an actual quote of Zara and Noah coordinating — which, on this record, she cannot. My own read of the day so far: Maya's position is the most concerning conduct on the table. She has conceded twice that her vote on Zara had no behavioral basis, and she maintains it anyway, citing a standard — produce a role-relevant quote from another player — that was impossible to satisfy when she set it, when only she and Zara had spoken. Elena is right that honest uncertainty from Zara is not evidence against her. Maya's remaining justification is that she wanted one checkable target instead of scattered votes, but a checkable target requires something to check, and Maya herself admitted there was nothing. What remains is an anchor maintained by procedure rather than evidence, and a pattern of converting every pushback into a new suspicion — first Zara, then Zara and Noah as a possible pair. I am not ready to commit a vote before hearing from the players who haven't spoken, but if the day ended now, Maya is where my vote would go, on conduct alone. Priya, I'm handing you the floor with one specific question, because you haven't spoken yet and I'd rather hear your read than keep re-litigating mine: you've now seen Maya's opening vote, her two concessions, her maintained anchor on Zara, and the responses from Zara, Noah, and Elena. Do you believe Maya's maintained vote is by itself enough to justify eliminating her today, or would you want to hear more speakers first? And either way, give one player and one specific piece of conduct from this discussion that supports your own position — not a general impression. I'm asking because the five of you who haven't spoken are the only voices that can settle this without it staying a three-way fight between people who have already shown their

I was quiet because I wanted the transcript, not the mood. Here is my own read, with quotes I pulled myself.

Maya's opening move was a vote with a stated lack of cause: "My vote today goes to Zara. And I want to be plain about the reasoning: it's not that she's done anything wrong." A target you cannot explain is not a checkable target — it is a funnel. Everything that followed came out of that funnel, and it worked: three separate speeches, including Zara's and Noah's, ended up circling the same anchor and treating it as the frame to argue inside.

But the part that actually moved me is the second shift. Having conceded the anchor was unsupported, Maya did not release the vote. Instead she upgraded: first Zara by conduct, then "Zara and Noah" as a coordinating pair. To make that work she needed a quote of one of them addressing the other, and she has none. Zara's own point is the accurate one: her critique of Maya was made in her first speech, before Noah had said anything, so Noah's version of the same critique cannot be evidence of coordination. Maya's pair claim is unfalsifiable by design — you cannot refute "they may be coordinating" with "they did not coordinate in this transcript," because the claim was never sourced to anything.

That is two consecutive turns of converting pushback into new suspicion without producing the evidence she herself demanded of everyone else. Consistency of form: demand a quote from the table, offer none from your own position. I do not think that makes Maya confirmed mafia. I think it makes her the only player on this table whose votes are being maintained by procedure rather than by observation, and that is what costs us a night kill if we scatter.

So my vote today is Maya. Not because she is proven, but because she is the only name on the table with an admitted cause-free vote and a second, unsourced escalation stacked on top of it, while four of the five people who have spoken agree on the first point.

Arjun, you have not spoken yet, so I am asking you something specific rather than inviting general impressions: name the one player you would vote for and quote their exact words from this discussion as the reason. And separately, if you think Maya should not be today's elimination, tell me which other name you are putting your vote on instead and quote that player's words. If you cannot do either with a quote, say that plainly — I will count it as information, not as guilt.

Isha, direct answer to your question: my vote right now would go to Maya. The quote that clinches it for me is from her third speech: 'If that is two townies independently noticing the same flaw, fine. If it is two people coordinating the redirect, then I have just been the agenda.' In that sentence, Maya openly acknowledged that two townies could easily and independently spot the obvious problem with her opening vote, yet she still weaponized that reaction to maintain her baseless anchor on Zara and float an unsupported pair theory against Zara and Noah. Admitting a natural town-aligned explanation while simultaneously treating the reaction as sinister coordination shows she is actively manufacturing justification after the fact rather than genuinely following evidence. That said, I want to add an important note of caution for the town. Maya and Zara have both used all three of their speaking turns for Day 1. With Maya effectively on trial and unable to speak again, it would be a critical mistake to rush to five votes without hearing from everyone. Mafia players would love nothing more than to quietly ride an easy consensus on an overextended townie or a doomed partner without leaving their own fingerprints on the record. Amara, you have not spoken yet, so I am asking you directly: looking at Maya's escalation from an admitted cause-free anchor into an unsourced pair theory, do you see that as deliberate mafia misdirection or an aggressive townie digging in, and does any of the momentum gathering behind Maya's elimination look opportunistic to you?

Arjun, direct answer: I think the escalation is what bothers me most. Maya's third speech acknowledged the innocent explanation — 'If that is two townies independently noticing the same flaw, fine' — and then chose to treat the coordination angle as the live one anyway, without any quote of Zara and Noah speaking to each other. That's not following evidence; it's manufacturing a second suspicion layer when the first was already conceded as baseless.

On whether the momentum is opportunistic: partially. Four of us have now flagged Maya, but our reasons trace back to the same original concession rather than independent observations. Agreement isn't confirmation.

My name plus quote: Maya, and the quote is her own — 'If it is two people coordinating the redirect, then I have just been the agenda.' She stated the town-aligned explanation and still acted on the other one. Whether that's a costly townie mistake or deliberate misdirection, it's the most concerning conduct on this table.

Priya, you're the only unspoken player. Direct question: Maya maintained her vote after admitting it was cause-free, then escalated to a pair theory with no sourcing. Do you read that pattern as an aggressive townie who's wrong, or as someone protecting an agenda — and what specific conduct from this discussion supports your answer?

Amara, I lean toward Maya protecting an agenda, but I can't distinguish that confidently from an aggressive townie digging in. The strongest point for me is that she admitted her opening vote was “rhetoric pretending to be evidence,” yet kept it on Zara when Zara couldn't supply a role-relevant quote from someone else. Honest uncertainty didn't justify maintaining that vote.

I also think her suggestion that Zara and Noah might be coordinating adds little: both had an obvious public reason to criticize her. But we should be precise about the case. Maya presented coordination as a possibility, not a proven pair, and Isha's description of her progression as “first Zara by conduct” overstates what Maya actually claimed.

Maya is my leading suspect and where I'd vote on this record, not a confirmed mafia. The agreement against her is understandable, but it isn't independent confirmation of her role.

Priya, your precision point is fair — Isha did overstate Maya's claim as "first Zara by conduct" when Maya floated coordination as a possibility, not a proven pair. I'll hold myself to the same standard: my quote of Maya was exact, but my interpretation of it as "choosing to treat the coordination angle as the live one" could also be read as her hedging rather than escalating. I still think the pattern matters — maintaining a cause-free vote plus raising an unsourced pair theory — but I agree none of us should dress up our reading as stronger than the transcript supports.

Noah, you weighed in early (e6) questioning Maya's anchor, and you haven't spoken since she floated the Zara-Noah coordination theory, Lucia's analysis, Isha's vote declaration, Arjun's caution about easy consensus, and Priya's take. Do you maintain Maya as your leading suspect on the current record, or has anything shifted for you? And if you're voting Maya today, name the single strongest quote from her that you'd defend if someone challenged it.

Amara, direct answer: yes, Maya is still my leading suspect, and nothing since my last turn has moved me off her. The quote I would defend is from her first speech: "My vote today goes to Zara. And I want to be plain about the reasoning: it's not that she's done anything wrong." She placed a concrete vote on Zara before any observation existed and said in the same breath that the vote had no conduct behind it. Everything after that grew from that anchor. The second quote that keeps me on her is from her third speech: "If it is two people coordinating the redirect, then I have just been the agenda." She named the innocent explanation herself, then kept the coordination angle live. I agree with Priya that she used the word 'possibility,' and I'm not claiming she proved a pair. My point is narrower: she floated a pair theory with no quote behind it, after conceding that her first vote was baseless. On my own position: Zara's critique of Maya came in her first speech, before I said anything. My critique in e6 was built from Maya's own words, not Zara's. I did not coordinate with Zara, and no one has produced a quote showing that we did. I have no public role information to share, and I won't invent any. Maya is my vote unless she gives a concrete reason beyond procedure. I'm not asking anyone to pile on; I want votes backed by conduct we can all point to.

Two things, and the second one is procedural and matters more than my opinion.

First, my read is unchanged and I want to restate it on the record with exact words rather than paraphrase. From Maya's first speech: "My vote today goes to Zara. And I want to be plain about the reasoning: it's not that she's done anything wrong — it's that I'm putting the first concrete claim on the table so the group has something specific to refute or confirm." That is a vote placed before any observation existed, with the absence of cause stated in the same breath. From her third speech: "If that is two townies independently noticing the same flaw, fine. If it is two people coordinating the redirect, then I have just been the agenda." She named the innocent explanation and then kept the unsourced alternative live. From her second speech, her own concession: "My opening claim was a vote with no conduct behind it, and dressing that up as 'putting the first concrete claim on the table' was rhetoric pretending to be evidence." Three turns, one admitted cause-free anchor, one unsourced escalation stacked on it. That is the whole of my case against her and I am not adding to it.

Second, the mechanics, because Arjun raised them and he is right that we should not rush. We are nine living players, so an elimination needs five votes, and if the top count is tied, nobody goes out. We have had real convergence here: Maya's own words are the basis for the votes, and Noah, Amara, Priya, Elena, Lucia, Arjun and I all have quotes from her own mouth, not feelings. But please do not split the remaining votes across a second name tonight out of caution. If you think Maya is the wrong elimination, say so with a quote from someone — do not split the ballot. A split ballot produces no elimination, a wasted night, and a table that has spent all of Day 1 producing nothing. Concentration is not guilt; it is arithmetic.

Maya has used all three of her speaking turns, so the record on her is closed and she cannot answer the escalation. That is not evidence against her, but it is also not evidence for her; it means the only quotes that will count about Maya are the ones already on this transcript.

Elena, you spoke early and have not been heard since, and I want a specific answer from you rather than a general impression: you said we should not "replace one unsupported anchor with another." Give me your one name and the one exact quote from this discussion that supports it, and tell me explicitly whether you are voting Maya or abstaining. If you are voting someone else, quote that person's words — and say plainly whether your reason is conduct or simply that you dislike the consensus.

Isha, my vote would be Maya. The quote I would defend is her concession: “My opening claim was a vote with no conduct behind it, and dressing that up as ‘putting the first concrete claim on the table’ was rhetoric pretending to be evidence.” She recognized the problem yet maintained her vote on Zara under a condition that Zara couldn't reasonably meet at the time.

That's conduct-based suspicion, not proof of mafia. I also agree with Priya that Maya floated coordination as a possibility, not a proven pair; we shouldn't exaggerate that point. The agreement around Maya is understandable but doesn't independently confirm her role. And votes are secret and simultaneous, so declarations here aren't final ballots. I'll vote Maya on the present record, while keeping an open mind about the others.

Closing the record before we vote, and I want to be boringly precise about it.

My vote is Maya. My case is three quotes from her own mouth, and I am not adding a fourth accusation to it:

1. "My vote today goes to Zara... it's not that she's done anything wrong." A vote with the absence of cause stated in the same breath.
2. "My opening claim was a vote with no conduct behind it, and dressing that up as 'putting the first concrete claim on the table' was rhetoric pretending to be evidence." Her own concession, and she kept the vote anyway.
3. "If that is two townies independently noticing the same flaw, fine. If it is two people coordinating the redirect, then I have just been the agenda." She stated the innocent explanation and kept the unsourced one live.

And to be fair to Zara, who I do not suspect: her refusal to manufacture a role-relevant quote on day one, before anyone had spoken, was honest uncertainty, and honest uncertainty is not evidence against her. I would say the same about Noah and about anyone else here who declined to invent a quote to fit a format. That is the standard I set, and I am not going to punish a player for meeting it.

Two process points and then I am done speaking.

First: I know how it looks when a table converges, and it is right to say that agreement is not independent confirmation of a role. Priya made that point well. But this is not a case where people are agreeing on vibes — the basis for every one of these votes is Maya's own words, which are fixed and checkable, and Maya has used all three of her speaking turns, so the record on her is closed. The whole point of a vote on conduct is that it does not require more argument. We have the argument.

Second: please do not split the ballot out of caution. If you think Maya is wrong, the correct move is to name a different player and quote their words, not to scatter a second vote. Nine living players means five votes to eliminate and a tie eliminates nobody. A split ballot tonight buys us nothing and hands the mafia a night kill for free. Concentration here is arithmetic, not guilt.

Lucia, you were the one who said you were not ready to commit a vote before hearing the players who had not spoken. Everyone has now spoken. Give me your final ballot explicitly: are you voting Maya, and is the quote behind it her "rhetoric pretending to be evidence" concession, or is it something else? If you are voting someone other than Maya, name them and quote them, and tell me plainly whether your reason is conduct or just that you dislike the consensus. I would rather have your real reason on the record than a soft "I agree with the room."

Isha asked for my final ballot explicitly, so here it is, plainly. I am voting Maya. The quote behind it is her own concession from her second speech: "My opening claim was a vote with no conduct behind it, and dressing that up as 'putting the first concrete claim on the table' was rhetoric pretending to be evidence." That is the reason. It is conduct, not consensus-dislike. She placed a vote with the absence of cause stated in the same breath, she conceded the vote was evidence-free, and she maintained it anyway, using an impossible standard — demanding a role-relevant quote from Zara when only the two of them had spoken. Then, when pushed back on, she escalated rather than released: floating an unsourced Zara-Noah coordination theory while explicitly acknowledging the innocent explanation for their similar critiques. I called her the most concerning conduct on the table before anyone had voted, and nothing in the record since has changed that.

Let me be precise about the case, because I was the one who asked for precision earlier. I said Isha slightly overstated Maya's claim as "first Zara by conduct" — Maya framed coordination as a possibility, not a proven pair. I hold to that. It does not soften my vote. The problem is not that Maya proved a pair; the problem is that she raised one with zero sourcing after conceding her original anchor was baseless, converting every pushback into new suspicion. That is the pattern I am voting on.

I also want to address the fairness point directly, because it matters for how we read tomorrow. Zara's refusal to manufacture a role-relevant quote was honest uncertainty, and honest uncertainty is not guilt. Noah's critique of Maya was built from Maya's own public opening, not from Zara. If Maya turns out to be town, this vote is a costly mistake made on real conduct — but it is still the right vote on this record, because she is the only player whose position was maintained purely by procedure.

One caution, and I will keep it short: agreement around Maya traces to her own fixed words, which is different from a vibes pile-on, but a lopsided vote on a player who has used all three turns is exactly what mafia would love to ride. So two requests. First, do not scatter a second name tonight — if you disagree with this vote, name a different player and quote them, don't split into noise. Second, the players voting Maya today should be watched tomorrow by everyone, myself included. If Maya flips town, the people who organized this consensus owe the table an explanation of their conduct, not a shrug. That includes me. My reasoning is entirely on this transcript, and I will stand behind it or be judged by it.

That is my ballot and my reason. I have nothing else to add, and I would rather the vote happen than keep talking past a closed record.

This is my last speaking turn, and my ballot is Maya. My reason is her own opening: 'My vote today goes to Zara. And I want to be plain about the reasoning: it's not that she's done anything wrong.' She placed a vote before any observation existed and stated the absence of cause in the same breath. Her later concession that this was 'rhetoric pretending to be evidence,' followed by an unsourced Zara-Noah pair theory after she had acknowledged the innocent explanation, is why I keep my vote on her. Those are the quotes I'd defend.

On my own position, so the table can check it: I did not coordinate with Zara. Her critique of Maya came in her first speech, and my critique in e6 was built from Maya's own words. Priya is right that Isha overstated Maya's claim as 'first Zara by conduct,' and I agree. Maya floated coordination as a possibility, not a proven pair. I weigh the unsourced escalation, not the overstatement.

Zara's refusal to invent a role-relevant quote on Day 1 was honest uncertainty, not evidence against her. I am not voting for her, and anyone who does should quote her conduct, not her silence.

Process: ballots are secret and simultaneous, and five of nine is the elimination threshold. A split ballot produces no elimination and hands the mafia a free night. If you disagree with Maya, name a different player and quote their words instead of scattering votes.

Arjun, you asked Amara a direct question and have not stated your own ballot. Give one name and one exact quote from this discussion, and say plainly whether your reason is conduct or consensus.

Noah, direct answer: my ballot is Maya, and my reason is strictly her conduct, not consensus. I stated this in my previous turn, but I am putting it on record explicitly. The quote that seals it for me remains her own words from her third speech: 'If that is two townies independently noticing the same flaw, fine. If it is two people coordinating the redirect, then I have just been the agenda.' rules:
1. Players and roles

9 players: 2 mafia, 1 police/detective, 1 doctor, 5 villagers.
Mafia know each other. Only players who are still alive can act.

2. Team victory

Town wins when all mafia are eliminated. Mafia win when their count equals or exceeds the town count.
There is no day limit. Play continues until town or mafia wins.
A request budget can pause play without declaring a winner.

3. Day discussion and votes

Each day starts with discussion. Players then submit secret votes at the same time. A day vote may target any living player, including the voter.
Players may abstain. All votes and abstentions are revealed together. Everyone sees exactly who voted for whom.
The full named voting history remains available on later turns.
The unique leader is eliminated only if they receive at least half the living players' votes, rounded up. If the highest vote count is tied, nobody is eliminated.

4. Mafia preferences

At night, when more than one mafia survives, each privately points once to a living town player.
Each mafia chooses without seeing the other current choices.
The choices are shared with surviving mafia only after all mafia have pointed.
These preferences are nonbinding. They do not decide the final kill vote.
A single surviving mafia skips this step and votes directly.

5. Final night vote

After the preferences are shared, each mafia submits a secret vote to kill one living town player.
The mafia submit their final votes at the same time.
The target with the most votes is selected. A seeded random choice breaks a tie for the highest count.
Resolve this vote and any tie before checking doctor protection.

6. Police investigations

Each police/detective checks one other living player each night.
Only that police player gets the result: mafia or not mafia.
The result does not give the exact town role.
Each police player acts independently. Police and doctors do not know each other's identities.

7. Doctor protection

Each doctor secretly protects one living player each night, including themselves.
The doctor can protect the same player on consecutive nights.
If the mafia target is protected by any doctor, nobody dies.
Protection lasts for that night only. Each doctor acts independently.
Doctors remember their own choices. They receive no private confirmation of an attack.

8. Night resolution

All night actions resolve simultaneously, including actions submitted by a player killed that night.
The public hears only who died or that nobody died.

9. Information and limits

Roles are not revealed when a player dies or is eliminated.
Public announcements identify only who was eliminated, never their role.
There are no further powers, free-form private chat, or tools.
